findings.title: update() uses organization-aware wrapper for login invalidation, missing invalidations when org disabled
findings.body: update() loads the original with getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false when its organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() decides with getLoginPredicate() which includes isEnabled(), so for an IdP in a disabled org both original and updated test as non-login. Changes to hideOnLogin, linkOnly or brokerPublic while the org is disabled therefore skip invalidation, leaving stale internalIds in the .idp.login caches. After the org is re-enabled OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), so a now-hidden, link-only or non-public broker from the stale list is displayed on the login page.

findings.title: Generic login paths re-check only isEnabled, allowing stale hidden brokers to show
findings.body: The specific-organization branch filters organization brokers by isEnabled() and !isLinkOnly() and !isHideOnLogin() and brokerPublic. The ORG_ONLY-without-org and ALL branches that use cached getForLogin() filter only by isEnabled(). If the login cache is stale or racy for hideOnLogin, linkOnly or brokerPublic, those stale IdPs remain in the cached id set, resolve successfully via getById(), pass the isEnabled() check, and are rendered on the login page when they should be hidden.

findings.title: Test cleanup uses literal "alias" instead of created alias, leaking IdPs
findings.body: The new test creates idp-alias-0..20 in a loop but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias" instead of the loop variable. That cleanup removes nothing, so 20+ brokers remain in the realm. Leftover brokers pollute counts asserted in the same test (5/6/10/11) and any later tests using the realm, causing flakiness. Same pattern appears for org-idp creation and idp-alias-20.

findings.title: removeAll() does not invalidate login caches
findings.body: removeAll() only registers invalidation for the count key and delegates, leaving realm .idp.login.* entries and org-id list queries in the cache. If removeAll() is ever called without deleting the realm, subsequent getForLogin() returns deleted brokers. It should invalidate login keys the same way create/remove do.
